To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a new training method that produces robust networks against parameter perturbation.
we propose a novel training method that promotes robust performance of NN models to random parameter noise, and that this approach is more effective than previous methods.
we introduce a new training algorithm for neural networks, which promotes robustness to parameter variation, and that our approach produces more robust neural networks than previous approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of robustness in the presence of parameter noise, and the development of new techniques to train networks that exhibit this property.
the problem of training neural networks that are robust to random mismatch and process variation, and to targeted parameter attacks during inference.
the development of robust neural network architectures that can be trained on a conventional GPU, and then deployed to a range of novel computational substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present a new training method that promotes parameter robustness in NN architectures, by introducing a regularization loss term that penalizes susceptibility to parameter noise.

we present a new training algorithm for robust neural networks, and show that our approach outperforms previous approaches for producing robust networks, in terms of robustness and computational cost.
we have developed a new method for training neural network architectures that is robust against parameter variation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed training method can produce networks that are robust to parameter variation, by promoting a flatter loss landscape during training.
we present a novel training algorithm that produces networks that are robust to random parameter variation during inference.
we present a novel approach to train networks that have robustness against parameter mismatch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that it is possible to train networks to be robust to parameter noise during inference.
the network architecture itself can be designed to be robust to parameter variation.
the network architecture and parameters can be designed to be robust to computational non-ideality, and that our method provides an efficient and effective approach to do so.
